# Fields

<!-- auto-generated by cmd/docgen — do not edit -->

Jira fields are metadata attributes on issues. Beyond system fields (summary,
status, assignee…), projects often define custom fields such as story points,
story type, team, or environment.

## jira field list

List all available fields for a project.

**Alias:** `ls`

### Usage

```
jira field list [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project` | `-p` | Project key |
| `--type` | | Filter by field type: `custom`, `system` |
| `--search` | | Search by field name |

### Inherited Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--context` | `-c` | Active Jira context name |
| `--json` | | Output in JSON format |
| `--yaml` | | Output in YAML format |

### Examples

```bash
jira field list
jira field list --type custom --json
jira field list --search "story points"
```

---

## jira field view

Display details and allowed values for a field.

### Usage

```
jira field view <field-id-or-name> [flags]
```

### Examples

```bash
jira field view story_points
jira field view customfield_10016 --json
```

---

## Field IDs in Custom Commands

When using `jira issue create` or `jira issue edit` with custom fields, use the
`--custom` flag:

```bash
# Set story points (customfield_10016)
jira issue edit MYPROJ-42 --custom customfield_10016=5

# Set a select field
jira issue edit MYPROJ-42 --custom customfield_10100="Team Alpha"

# Set a date field
jira issue edit MYPROJ-42 --custom customfield_10200=2024-03-01

# Multiple custom fields
jira issue edit MYPROJ-42 \
  --custom customfield_10016=3 \
  --custom customfield_10100="Backend"
```

Get field IDs with:

```bash
jira field list --type custom --json | jq '.[] | {id, name}'
```
